title: 103學年度指定科目考試英文考科

parts.title: 第貳部分：非選擇題（占28分）
parts.instructions: 說明：本部分共有二題，請依各題指示作答，答案必須寫在「答案卷」上，並標明大題號（一、二）。作答務必使用筆尖較粗之黑色墨水的筆書寫，且不得使用鉛筆。

sections.title: 一、詞彙（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第1題至第10題，每題有4個選項，其中只有一個是正確或最適當的選項，請畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得1分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

questions.stem: When dining at a restaurant, we need to be ______ of other customers and keep our conversations at an appropriate noise level.
John shows ______ towards his classmates. He doesn’t take part in any of the class activities and doesn’t even bother talking to other students in his class.
To meet the unique needs of the elderly, the company designed a cell phone ______ for seniors, which has big buttons and large color displays.
A well-constructed building has a better chance of ______ natural disasters such as typhoons, tornadoes, and earthquakes.
Our family doctor has repeatedly warned me that spicy food may ______ my stomach, so I’d better stay away from it.
Because the new principal is young and inexperienced, the teachers are ______ about whether he can run the school well.
Many universities offer a large number of scholarships as an ______ to attract outstanding students to enroll in their schools.
Since Diana is such an ______ speaker, she has won several medals for her school in national speech contests.
The candidate made energy ______ the central theme of his campaign, calling for a greater reduction in oil consumption.
Concerned about mudslides, the local government quickly ______ the villagers from their homes before the typhoon hit the mountain area.

sections.title: 二、綜合測驗（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第11題至第20題，每題一個空格，請依文意選出最適當的一個選項，請畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得1分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
Brushing your teeth regularly will help you maintain a healthy smile. But that smile won’t last long if you don’t take proper care of your toothbrush and switch to a new one often. According to the American Dental Association (ADA), toothbrushes can harbor bacteria. These germs come from the mouth and can [[11]] in toothbrushes over time.
Many Americans replace their toothbrushes only once or twice a year. The ADA, however, recommends [[12]] a new toothbrush every three to four months. Children’s toothbrushes may need to be changed more [[13]].
During those three to four months of use, there are several ways to keep a toothbrush clean. [[14]], rinse your toothbrush thoroughly with tap water after use, making sure to remove any toothpaste and debris. Store your toothbrush in an upright position, and let [[15]] air dry. Most importantly, do not share toothbrushes.

tags.key_phrase: let it air dry (it = your toothbrush)

groups.passage:
Hiding herself among the trees near a chimpanzee habitat, Elizabeth Lonsdorf is using her camera to explore mysteries of learning. The chimpanzee she records picks up a thin flat piece of grass and then digs out tiny insects from a hole. Dinner is [[16]]! But how did the chimp develop this ingenious skill with tools? Do the chimp babies copy their parents in using tools? Do the mothers most skilled with tools have offspring who are also good at using tools? Here in Africa, Lonsdorf is conducting one of the world’s longest wildlife studies, trying to discover how learning is transferred [[17]] generations.
Lonsdorf has always been interested in animal learning and tool use, [[18]] the way young animals grow up and learn their way in the world. Her chimpanzee study shows a clear link between humans and the rest of the animal kingdom. The chimps make and use tools and have mother-child relationships very [[19]] to those of humans. Through observing chimpanzees’ learning process, researchers hope to gain insight into what the development of our earliest ancestors [[20]] like.
Lonsdorf hopes that by understanding the complexity of animal behavior, we can better appreciate and protect the diversity of life on this planet.

tags.key_phrase: might have + p.p.（對過去的推測）

tags.topic: a long-term study of how chimpanzees learn to use tools

sections.title: 三、文意選填（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明：第21題至第30題，每題一個空格，請依文意在文章後所提供的(A)到(L)選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其英文字母代號畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得1分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
The practice of burning paper money or paper model offerings at funerals in Chinese society can be traced back to the Tang dynasty (618-907 AD). Chinese people believe that when someone passes away, there is a death of the body, but the [[21]] continues to live in the next world. This “next world” is a mirror of the human world, where the “residents” need places to live, money to spend, daily necessities, and entertainment just like when they were [[22]]. Some of these necessities are buried with the deceased, while most others are “shipped” to them by burning paper models. As the ashes fly high, the offerings are [[23]] by the residents in the next world.
Relatives of the deceased want to see their beloved family members live comfortably in the next world, so the paper houses are big and the cars are very [[24]], mostly Mercedes-Benzes. A complete package of paper offerings may include a couple of servants, cash, and credit cards so that the deceased will have all their [[25]] satisfied.
These traditional paper offerings were sold only at specialty stores in the past. The style and variety of the products were [[26]]. For example, “houses” looked all the same and were built by pasting paper around a bamboo frame, with [[27]] of a door, windows, and a roof printed on it. There were no trendy, modern supplies to choose from. Now, the [[28]] can be made on the Internet. And with the incorporation of new materials and designs, paper offerings come in many more varieties. The old one-style-fits-all houses have been [[29]] by buildings that are fully equipped with decorations, furniture, and household appliances. Digital cameras, iPhones, and even skin care products are also [[30]]. It seems that, with the help of a simple click, this old Chinese tradition has been given a face-lift.

sections.title: 四、篇章結構（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明：第31題至第35題，每題一個空格。請依文意在文章後所提供的(A)到(F)選項中分別選出最適當者，填入空格中，使篇章結構清晰有條理，並將其英文字母代號畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得2分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
Eccentrics are people who have an unusual or odd personality, set of beliefs, or behavior pattern. They may or may not comprehend the standards for normal behavior in their culture. They simply don’t care about the society’s disapproval of their habits or beliefs.
Once considered socially unacceptable, eccentric people have been found to possess some positive characteristics. [[31]] They often have more curiosity about the world and, in many cases, are contentedly obsessed by hobbies and interests. [[32]] They live in a world of their own and do not worry about what others think of them. So they are usually less restricted and therefore more carefree in forming new ideas.
[[33]] Statistics show they visit their doctors less—about once in eight to nine years, which is 20 times less than the average person. This could be partly due to their innate traits such as humor and happiness. [[34]] This may explain why eccentrics are, on the whole, healthier.
Psychologists therefore suggest that we pay attention to those who do not conform. It could be our aunt who has been raising pet lizards. [[35]] Their crazy hobby or strange sense of humor is what keeps them going. Eccentric people may seem odd, but they will likely live a happier and healthier life because they enjoy what they are doing. In fact, many of history’s most brilliant minds have displayed some unusual behaviors and habits.

options_bank.A: Eccentrics are also found to be healthier.
options_bank.B: According to a recent study in England, eccentrics are more creative.
options_bank.C: Or it could be our best friend’s brother who wears shorts to a formal dance.
options_bank.D: People may have eccentric taste in clothes, or have eccentric hobbies.
options_bank.E: Psychologists also find that eccentric people do not follow conventions.
options_bank.F: Such personal traits are found to play an important role in boosting the body’s immune system.

tags.topic: positive traits of eccentric people: creativity and health

sections.title: 五、閱讀測驗（占32分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第36題至第51題，每題請分別根據各篇文章之文意選出最適當的一個選項，請畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得2分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
Opened in 1883, the Brooklyn Bridge was the first long-span suspension bridge to carry motor traffic, and it quickly became the model for the great suspension bridges of the following century. Spanning New York’s East River, it provided the first traffic artery between Manhattan Island and Brooklyn. Before that, the only transportation was by ferries, which were slow and could be dangerous in winter.
The construction of a bridge over the East River had been discussed since the early 19th century, but the outbreak of the Civil War in 1861 deflected all consideration of the project. When the war ended in 1865, the bridge became an important issue once more. In 1867, the New York State legislature passed an act incorporating the New York Bridge Company for the purpose of constructing and maintaining a bridge between Manhattan Island and Brooklyn.
John Augustus Roebling was chosen to design the bridge. Born in Germany in 1806, he held radical views as a student and was listed by the German police as a dangerous liberal. He emigrated to America in 1830 to escape political discrimination.
Roebling proposed a bridge with a span of 1,500 feet (465 m), with two masonry towers in the East River serving as the main piers. The bridge that was actually built is longer—1,597 feet (486 m), the longest suspension bridge at that time.

questions.stem: What was the purpose of building the Brooklyn Bridge?

options.B: To set up a model for bridge construction.
options.C: To build a suspension bridge for the Civil War.
options.D: To provide faster and safer transportation than boats.

questions.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “deflected” in the second paragraph?

options.B: It is shorter than originally planned.
options.C: It was first proposed after the Civil War.
options.D: It was built by the New York Bridge Company.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following correctly describes John Augustus Roebling?

options.A: He participated in the Civil War and was seriously wounded.
options.B: He was chosen to design the bridge because of his radical views.
options.C: He was the first person to propose the construction of the bridge.
options.D: He moved to America because he was discriminated against in his home country.

tags.topic: history of the Brooklyn Bridge and its designer John Augustus Roebling

groups.passage:
The Japanese have long puzzled public health researchers because they are such an apparent paradox: They have the world’s lowest rates of heart disease and the largest number of people that live to or beyond 100 years despite the fact that most Japanese men smoke—and smoking counts as one of the strongest risk factors for heart disease. So what’s protecting Japanese men?
Two professors at the University of California at Berkeley hoped to find out the answer. They investigated a pool of 12,000 Japanese men equally divided into three groups: One group had lived in Japan for all their lives, and the other two groups had emigrated to Hawaii or Northern California. It was found that the rate of heart disease among Japanese men increased five times in California and about half of that for those in Hawaii.
The differences could not be explained by any of the usual risk factors for heart disease, such as smoking, high blood pressure, or cholesterol counts. The change in diet, from sushi to hamburgers and fries, was also not related to the rise in heart disease. However, the kind of society they had created for themselves in their new home country was. The most traditional group of Japanese Americans, who maintained tight-knit and mutually supportive social groups, had a heart-attack rate as low as their fellow Japanese back home. But those who had adopted the more isolated Western lifestyle increased their heart-attack incidence by three to five times.
The study shows that the need to bond with a social group is so fundamental to humans that it remains the key determinant of whether we stay healthy or get ill, even whether we live or die. We need to feel part of something bigger to thrive. We need to belong, not online, but in the real world of hugs, handshakes, and pats on the back.

questions.stem: What is the best title of this passage?

options.D: The Sense of Belonging vs. Isolation

questions.stem: Which of the following is a finding of the two American professors’ study?

options.A: Many Japanese men that lived up to 100 years were smokers.
options.B: Those who often ate hamburgers and fries were more likely to fall sick.
options.C: Japanese immigrants to America usually formed a tight-knit community.
options.D: Westernized social life was related to the heart-attack rate of Japanese Americans.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of “something bigger” in the last paragraph?
What is the ratio of heart disease between Japanese living in Japan and Japanese Americans in Hawaii?

tags.topic: social connection protecting Japanese men from heart disease

groups.passage:
Bitcoin is an experimental, decentralized digital currency that enables instant payments to anyone, anywhere in the world. Bitcoin uses peer-to-peer technology to operate with no central authority; that is, managing transactions and issuing money are carried out collectively through the network.
Any transaction issued with Bitcoin cannot be reversed; it can only be refunded by the person receiving the funds. That means you should do business with people and organizations you know and trust, or who have an established reputation. Bitcoin can detect typos and usually won’t let you send money to an invalid address by mistake.
All Bitcoin transactions are stored publicly and permanently on the network, which means anyone can see the balance and transactions of any Bitcoin address. However, the identity of the user behind an address remains unknown until information is revealed during a purchase or in other circumstances.
The price of a bitcoin can unpredictably increase or decrease over a short period of time due to its young economy, novel nature, and sometimes illiquid markets. Consequently, keeping your savings with Bitcoin is not recommended at this point. Bitcoin should be seen like a high risk asset, and you should never store money that you cannot afford to lose with Bitcoin. If you receive payments with Bitcoin, many service providers can convert them to your local currency.
Bitcoin is an experimental new currency that is in active development. Although it becomes less experimental as usage grows, you should keep in mind that Bitcoin is a new invention that is exploring ideas that have never been attempted before. As such, its future cannot be predicted by anyone.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of this article?

options.B: To prove the value of a young economy.
options.C: To explore ways to do online transactions.
options.D: To explain how to build up a business network.

questions.stem: Why is the value of Bitcoin not stable?

options.B: Because it is not a valid investment.
options.D: Because its circulation is limited to the youth.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about Bitcoin?

options.A: Bitcoin addresses are known only to their owners.
options.B: Once a transaction is made, the Bitcoin cannot be refunded.
options.C: Bitcoin user’s identity is always open to the general public.
options.D: When a payment is received, the Bitcoin can be turned into local currency.

questions.stem: What advice would the author give to those who are interested in keeping money in Bitcoin?

options.C: Make hay while the sun shines.

tags.topic: Bitcoin as an experimental digital currency

groups.passage:
Scientists are trying to genetically modify the world in which we live. They are even trying to wipe out diseases via genetic modification. For example, researchers have tried to engineer mosquitoes to kill malaria parasites. The malaria parasite is carried by the female Anopheles mosquito. When transmitted to a human, the parasite travels first to the liver and then on to the bloodstream, where it reproduces and destroys red blood cells. An estimated 250 million people suffer from malaria each year, and about one million die—many of them children. There are currently no effective or approved malaria vaccines.
To “kill” malaria, scientists are genetically modifying a bacterium in mosquitoes so that it releases toxic compounds. These compounds are not harmful to humans or the mosquito itself, but they do kill off the malaria parasite, making the mosquito incapable of infecting humans with malaria.
Despite this achievement, scientists are faced with the challenge of giving the modified mosquitoes a competitive advantage so that they can eventually replace the wild population. Complete blockage of the malaria parasite is very important. If some of the parasites slip through the mechanism, then the next generation will likely become resistant to it. And if that happens, the scientists are back where they started.
Another challenge for scientists is to gain public approval for this genetic modification regarding mosquitoes and malaria control. Environmental activists have raised concerns about the release of genetically engineered organisms without any clear knowledge of their long-term effect on ecosystems and human health. There is still a long way to go before genetic modification techniques are put to use in disease control.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.A: Researchers have found an effective way to halt the spread of insect-borne diseases around the world.
options.B: Many people are worried about the effects of genetically modified organisms on the environment.
options.C: It takes time to gain public support for the application of genetic modification to disease control.
options.D: Genetic engineering looks promising in reducing malaria, though there may be unknown consequences.

questions.stem: Which of the following best shows the organization of this passage?
According to the passage, which of the following is true about malaria parasites?

options.A: They are resistant to genetic modification and vaccines.
options.B: They reproduce in the human liver and grow stronger there.
options.C: They can be found in only one gender of a class of mosquitoes.
options.D: They are transmitted to around one million children each year.

questions.stem: What does “that” in the third paragraph refer to?

options.A: Some malaria parasites escaping from the ecosystems.
options.B: Malaria parasites becoming immune to the engineered bacterium.
options.C: Modified mosquitoes becoming more competitive than the wild ones.
options.D: Transmission of malaria being blocked from mosquitoes to humans.

tags.topic: genetically modifying mosquitoes to fight malaria

sections.instructions:
說明：1.請將以下中文句子譯成正確、通順、達意的英文，並將答案寫在「答案卷」上。

questions.label: 中譯英1
questions.stem: 食用過多油炸食物可能會導致學童體重過重，甚至更嚴重的健康問題。
questions.scoring_notes:
第一大題是「中譯英」，題型與過去幾年相同，考生須將兩個中文句子譯成正確、通順而達意的兩個英文句子，兩題共計八分。
關於評分標準，在中譯英部分，每小題總分 4 分，原則上是每個錯誤扣 0.5 分。
今年的中譯英與「食用過多油炸食物」有關，句型及詞彙皆在高中生所熟悉的範圍之內。評量的重點在於考生是否能運用所學的詞彙與基本句型將中文翻譯成正確、通順且達意的英文句子。由於測驗之詞彙皆控制在大考中心詞彙表四級內之詞彙，中等程度以上的考生如果能使用正確句型，並注意用字、拼字的準確度，應能得到理想的分數。但在選取樣卷時，仍發現以下的缺失：例如在拼字方面，有一些學生把 therefore 寫成 therefor；把 Eating 寫成 Eeating；把 solve 寫成 slove 等，我們認為這些拼字的錯誤，如果考生能在平常練習的時候多注意，應該是可以避免的。今年也有部分考生的翻譯直接以中文的結構表達，例如將「導致學童體重過重」翻譯成 “…cause the children’s weight too heavy”。此外也有部分考生漏譯了「過多」(too much) 的意思，而只譯成 more，或漏譯了「棘手」及「有效」兩個重要的形容詞，相當可惜。

patterns: 動名詞當主詞（Eating too much fried food ...）
tags.topic: eating too much fried food leading to overweight and health problems in schoolchildren

sections.title: 二、英文作文（占20分）
sections.instructions:
說明︰1.依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2.文長至少120個單詞（words）。

stats.source: stats-3.xls 工作表「2」英文科非選擇題各題分數人數統計表：第二題(滿分:20分)

figures.label: 下圖
figures.description: 作文提示下方的直條圖（無標題），呈現美國某高中全體學生每天進行各種活動的時間分配。縱軸刻度為 0、2、4、6、8、10，圖例「單位: 小時」。橫軸七個類別由左到右排列，類別標籤斜排並附數值：學習相關活動 6.4、打工 1.5、睡覺 8.7、社交、休閒 3.8、運動 0.8、宗教、義工 0.2、其他 2.6。直條高度與標示數值一致：睡覺最高（8.7 小時），學習相關活動次之（6.4 小時），社交、休閒 3.8 小時，其他 2.6 小時，打工 1.5 小時，運動 0.8 小時，宗教、義工最低（0.2 小時，直條幾乎貼近 0）。七項合計 24 小時。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem: 下圖呈現的是美國某高中的全體學生每天進行各種活動的時間分配，請寫一篇至少120個單詞的英文作文。文分兩段，第一段描述該圖所呈現之特別現象；第二段請說明整體而言，你一天的時間分配與該高中全體學生的異同，並說明其理由。
questions.scoring_notes:
第二大題是「引導式作文」，考生須從試卷提供的一個統計圖中找出相關資訊，以至少 120 個單詞（words），根據題目的提示，寫出一篇兩段的作文。作文部分滿分為二十分。
作文的評分標準是依據內容、組織、文法句構、字彙拼字、體例五個項目給分，字數明顯不足者扣總分 1 分。
今年作文題目的引導方式是文字加上一幅與考生的生活經驗息息相關的統計圖表。統計圖中呈現的是「美國某高中的全體學生每天進行各種活動的時間分配」數據，圖表中的資料均以中文說明，而且臺灣的學生在國中時都已學過如何閱讀這樣的統計表，所以今年的考生多能發揮。
考生作文應分兩段，第一段描述該圖所呈現之特別現象；第二段說明就整體而言，考生本人的時間分配與圖中顯示的高中全體學生時間分配之異同。從樣卷中發現：英文寫作能力中等以上之考生皆能針對上述兩個引導原則發揮其寫作能力及創意，能在第一段說明該圖所呈現之「特別現象」，再引伸說明這種現象與臺灣當前現象之不同處，以凸顯統計圖表資料特別之處。在第二段則比較說明自己的時間安排與圖表所示之異同，中等以上之考生應能把不同處寫出來。評分的考量重點為考生書寫的內容是否符合試題之圖、文引導與說明，組織是否完整，用字、拼字及句子結構是否正確，是否已把全文清楚地敘述出來等因素。

extraction.method: python-docx 讀 Word 版題本 paper-2.docx 為主（含 w:sym Wingdings F0E0 箭頭→U+2192、內嵌圖表 word/charts/chart1.xml 數據），pdftotext -layout 擷取 paper-1.pdf 逐詞比對，並用 Read 逐頁看 PDF 頁面影像（第 1–8 頁）核對版面、粗斜體與作文統計圖；答案 pdftotext answer.pdf＋頁面影像核對；評分原則 pdftotext scoring.pdf（-layout 與 -raw）＋頁面影像（2 頁）核對；統計以 xlrd 讀 stats-1.xls（英：P/Ph/Pl/D）、stats-2.xls（英：T/H/L 選項分析）、stats-3.xls（工作表 2：英文科非選擇題分數人數統計）；建檔腳本放 scratchpad，未進 repo
issues: 結構與 gsat-spec.json legacy_ast「98–110」期別一致：詞彙 1–10（各1分；103 題本標為「詞彙」而非「詞彙題」，與 spec 註記「100及107–110題本標為詞彙題」相符）、綜合測驗 11–20（2篇×5題）、文意選填 21–30（12個選項 A–L）、篇章結構 31–35（6個選項 A–F，各2分）、閱讀測驗 36–51（4篇×4題，各2分）、中譯英 2題各4分、英文作文 20分（至少120個單詞，文分兩段）；選擇題 72分＋非選擇題 28分＝100分；考試時間 80分鐘（封面）；不倒扣（各題說明：答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算）。評分原則寫明作文依「內容、組織、文法句構、字彙拼字、體例五個項目給分」，與 spec changes「105：英文作文評分由五項（含體例）改為四項」相符。
非選擇題題號：題本中譯英子題編為 1、2，英文作文不編號；因 schema 要求 no 為整數，中譯英填 no=1、2（label「中譯英1」「中譯英2」），作文填 no=1（label「英文作文」），因此 validator 出現「題號重複 [1, 2]」warning，label 皆不重複，屬合理（同 ast-105、ast-107、ast-110 慣例）。

中譯英：評分原則（scoring.pdf）沒有公布參考譯文，也沒有列出可接受譯法，兩題 answer 與 accepted_answers 均為 null。scoring_notes 逐字收錄三段：首段「第一大題是「中譯英」，…兩題共計八分。」（取自首段介紹非選擇題的句子中屬於中譯英的分句）、評分標準句「關於評分標準，在中譯英部分，每小題總分 4 分，原則上是每個錯誤扣 0.5 分。」、以及「今年的中譯英與「食用過多油炸食物」有關…相當可惜。」整段。該段各句同時涉及兩題、無法切開（拼字錯誤 therefore→therefor、solve→slove 與漏譯「棘手」「有效」屬第2題；Eating→Eeating、「導致學童體重過重」直譯、漏譯「過多」(too much) 屬第1題），因此兩題 scoring_notes 內容相同。評分原則中閱卷籌備流程（7月7日、7月9日會議）與「每份試卷皆會經過兩位委員分別評分…」的閱卷流程說明不屬於個別題目，未收錄。

英文作文：answer 為 null（評分原則沒有範文）；scoring_notes 逐字收錄首段中屬於作文的分句「第二大題是「引導式作文」，…作文部分滿分為二十分。」、評分標準句「作文的評分標準是依據內容、組織、文法句構、字彙拼字、體例五個項目給分，字數明顯不足者扣總分 1 分。」以及評分原則最後兩段作文說明（全文）。stem 為題本「下圖呈現的是…並說明其理由。」整段（本卷沒有「提示：」標籤）。essay_type 標 chart（依統計圖寫作，同 ast-108），paragraphs 2，word_requirement「at least 120 words」。

作文統計圖（s7g1 figures[0]）：題本第7頁（PDF 第8頁）的直條圖沒有標題，故 caption 為 null、label「下圖」。內容依頁面影像與 Word 檔內嵌圖表 word/charts/chart1.xml 的數據雙重確認：縱軸刻度 0–10（間隔2），圖例「單位: 小時」（半形冒號加空白，照原文），七個類別標籤本身含數值並斜排：學習相關活動 6.4、打工 1.5、睡覺 8.7（XML 存為 8.6999999999999993，標籤印 8.7）、社交、休閒 3.8、運動 0.8、宗教、義工 0.2、其他 2.6；七項合計 24 小時。rows 第一列「活動類別／每天時間（小時）」為解析者所加的欄名。

非選擇題統計：stats-3.xls 工作表「2」只提供「第一題（中譯英兩小題合計，滿分8分）」與「第二題（英文作文，滿分20分）」的分數人數分布，無逐子題資料，也沒有答對率／鑑別度；因此放在 s6、s7 section 層級的 stats（schema 未定義的延伸欄位：source、max_score、registered、absent、examinees、percent_base、score_distribution，同 ast-105、ast-107），題目層級 stats 為 null。原表百分比以報名總人數 62,021（含缺考 3,035；到考 58,986，與 stats-1 表頭一致）為分母，已換成 0–1 小數（保留 4 位）；分數區間標籤去除空白（如「9.00- 9.99」→「9.00-9.99」），只收錄有數值的列。作文「20.00-20.99」一列原表明列人數 0，照錄；最低區間為「0.00-0.99」一列。

選擇題 stats：correct_rate／high_group／low_group／discrimination 取自 stats-1.xls「英」的 P、Ph、Pl、D；另加延伸欄位 omit_rate（未答比例）、option_rates_high／option_rates_low（高分組／低分組各選項選答比例），與 option_rates 同取自 stats-2.xls 的 T/H/L 列（同 ast-105）。已逐題核對 stats-2 標 * 的選項＝answer.pdf 官方答案（51題全部一致）；51題的 P＝T列正答比例、Ph＝H列正答比例，且 D＝Ph−Pl 全部成立。Pl 與 L 列正答比例有兩題差 1 個百分點：第21題 Pl 44 vs L 列 C 45、第39題 Pl 23 vs L 列 D 24（應為四捨五入差異），low_group 採 stats-1 的 Pl，option_rates_low 保留 stats-2 原值。原表為整數百分比，option_rates 加總因四捨五入與未答（0–2%）略偏離 1。
頂層 parts 為延伸欄位（同 ast-105、ast-107、ast-110），保存「第壹部分：選擇題（占72分）」「第貳部分：非選擇題（占28分）」標題與第貳部分的說明文字（逐字）；封面「作答注意事項」未收錄。
已逐頁看 PDF 頁面影像（第 1–8 頁）：全卷唯一的圖表是英文作文的統計直條圖；選擇題各題組沒有插圖、圖表或表格，figures 為空陣列。

題本格式依規定不保留：粗體 deflected（36–39 選文第二段與第37題）、something bigger（40–43 選文末段與第42題）、that（48–51 選文第三段與第51題），斜體 Anopheles，上標 19th 的 th（寫成 19th）。37、42、51 題問的是粗體字而非底線，故未加 <u>。注意第51題：選文第三段有兩個 that（“so that they can eventually replace…” 與 “And if that happens…”），粗體的是 “And if that happens” 的 that（顯示給學生時建議另行標示）。

Word 檔處理：第49題四個選項的箭頭在 Word 檔是 Wingdings 符號字（w:sym F0E0，python-docx 的 p.text 會漏掉、pdftotext 輸出為私用區 U+F0E0），依頁面影像改寫為 U+2192「→」（如 “Introduction → Comparison → Contrast”）；選文空格（底線＋題號）改寫為 [[題號]]，段落間以換行分隔；分頁符號、空段落、段首 tab（36–39 選文第二段）與行尾空白已去除。經 pdftotext -layout 逐詞比對，選擇題部分英文 2,974 個詞完全一致；另把所有選文段落、題幹、選項、說明文字、中譯英與作文題目共 230 段去除空白後，逐一確認為 PDF 文字的子字串（0 段不符）。

說明文字照 Word 檔原字元保留：詞彙、綜合測驗、閱讀測驗、英文作文的「說明︰」用 U+FE30 冒號，文意選填、篇章結構、中譯英與第貳部分用全形「：」；中譯英說明第2點在 Word 檔前面有三個全形空白（U+3000）、英文作文說明第2點前面有六個半形空白作縮排對齊，已去除並以換行分隔。英文作文 stem Word 檔寫「至少120個單詞」，PDF 排版顯示為「至少 120 個單詞」（自動中英間距），照 Word 檔。文意選填選項 PDF 印成「( I ) alive」「( J ) needs」（括號內有空白），代號仍為 I、J。

評分原則文字：pdftotext -layout 在個別行輸出字距空白（如「以 中 文 的 結 構 表 達 …」），改以 pdftotext -raw 與頁面影像核對；PDF 換行處中文直接相接，中文與英文／數字相接處依頁面影像保留一個空白（如「扣 0.5 分」「寫成 Eeating」「翻譯成 “…cause the children’s weight too heavy”」「只譯成 more」），並去除跨頁頁碼。本檔文字層沒有 CJK 相容表意文字。原文的半形括號「(too much)」與彎引號照錄。
